title: Sum the Fields of a Line Without Splitting
oneLiner: Add up the semicolon-separated numbers in a line by walking it with indexes and slicing a ReadOnlySpan<char>, instead of splitting it into new strings.
keyTakeaway: Split allocates an array plus a new string per field. Walking the text with IndexOf and parsing each slice of a ReadOnlySpan<char> straight away (int.Parse accepts spans) does the same job with no allocations at all, which matters when a parser runs millions of times. Python has no span for str, but the same index-walking logic applies.
explanation:
Write SumFields(line), which returns the sum of the integers in a line of fields separated by semicolons. "10;20;30" gives 60. Fields may have spaces around the number (" 7 ") and may be negative; empty fields, including a completely empty line, count as nothing, so "-5; 7 ;;8" gives 10 and "" gives 0. Every non-empty field is a valid int, and the totals fit in an int.

In C# the parameter is a ReadOnlySpan<char>, a view of the line's characters, so you can't call Split on it: find the next ';' with IndexOf, take the field as a slice (line[..end]), skip it if it's empty or only spaces (IsWhiteSpace() on the span), otherwise add int.Parse(field), which accepts a span and ignores surrounding spaces. Then continue with the rest of the line (line[(end + 1)..]). Nothing in your loop creates a string.

In Python, strings have no no-copy view, so the point is the logic rather than the memory: walk the line with line.find(";", start), take line[start:end] for each field, skip blank ones with strip(), and add int(field), which also ignores surrounding spaces. (In everyday Python, sum over line.split(";") is fine.)

visualizationSteps.message: The line "-5; 7 ;;8". A span is a view of these characters: slicing it moves the view, nothing is copied.
IndexOf(';') is 2, so the first field is line[..2], "-5". int.Parse reads it straight from the span: total -5.
Move past the ';' (line[3..]). The next field is " 7 "; int.Parse ignores the spaces: total 2.
The next field is empty (two semicolons in a row): skip it.
No more ';', so the rest of the line, "8", is the last field: total 10. No strings were created.

complexity.note: Each character is looked at a constant number of times (by IndexOf and by the parse), and slicing a span is O(1) with no copying, so only the running total is stored. Split would also be O(n) time but O(n) space for the array and substrings.
